item.title: When a European airline chooses to delay, they still must pay, ECJ rules
item.description: If a European airline chooses to delay a flight due to extraordinary circumstances, causing later flights to be delayed, it must compensate the subsequent passengers, according to a new European Court of Justice ruling on Wednesday.

item.title: Iran war shifts EU attention from ‘extreme’ Israeli actions in Gaza
item.description: The EU Parliament should — at the least — hold a plenary debate on Gaza to hold Israel to account despite the Iran crisis, leftwing, Green, and liberal groups told press in Brussels on Wednesday.

item.title: EU inches towards migration and investment pact with Senegal
item.description: Migration control is at the heart of a planned 'strategic partnership' between the EU and Senegal.

item.title: Listen: Will the new ‘Made in Europe’ doctrine revive the European industry?
item.description: After several years of industrial decline, the European Commission proposed a ‘Made in Europe’ policy. Is this a major industrial turning point?

item.title: With elections on 22 March, why is Slovenia sliding to the right?
item.description: A stable but flatlining economy, social tensions with Roma, welfare payments and emigrating medics, and a fragmented Left are all shaping the Slovenian electoral campaign, ahead of the parliamentary elections on 22 March.

item.title: Leak: EPP sparks row with rival deportation bill ahead of crucial parliament vote
item.description: "It has become evident that the necessary majority for a compromise has not materialised," the centre-right MEP François-Xavier Bellamy said in an email to his counterparts, seen by EUobserver, ahead of a vote on the controversial deportation bill.

item.title: EU under pressure to match US sanctions on Rwanda
item.description: The US Treasury imposed sanctions under its Global Magnitsky Act in the wake of the Rwandan army and the M23 militia group capturing the city of Ulvira in the South Kivu province of eastern DR Congo last year

item.title: Experts find holes in planned changes to EU landmark online privacy law
item.description: A major digital rights NGO found serious differences between the EU Commission’s proposed changes to the bloc's landmark General Data Protection Regulation — and what data professionals in the field really want altering.

item.title: 39 days to election: Orbán warns of a possible Ukrainian attack but rules out postponing election
item.description: In our regular digest of the week’s news from the Hungarian campaign trail: opinion polls, why Hungarian PM Orbán does not rule out deploying soldiers on the streets, claims Ukraine is financing the opposition Tisza party, and Tisza mobilises in the countryside.

item.title: EU and Gulf states urge Iran to halt attacks amid escalation risks
item.description: Asked if southern EU states were at risk of further aggression, EU commissioner Dubravka Šuica said: "It's not easy to anticipate at this moment, but I don't think it will happen".
